CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Passwords Configured to Never Expire
CustomReports.Description: Identifies accounts with the DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD flag enabled, which bypasses password aging policies.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Password Not Required Permitted
CustomReports.Description: Accounts where the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag allows blank or empty passwords.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Store Password Using Reversible Encryption
CustomReports.Description: Accounts configured to store passwords using reversible encryption, effectively storing plaintext-equivalent credentials.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Kerberos Pre-Authentication Disabled (AS-REP Roasting)
CustomReports.Description: Accounts vulnerable to AS-REP Roasting due to the DONT_REQ_PREAUTH flag.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Kerberoastable User Accounts with SPN
CustomReports.Description: Standard user accounts with registered Service Principal Names (SPNs) susceptible to offline ticket cracking.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] DES Encryption Only Enabled
CustomReports.Description: Accounts restricted to legacy 56-bit DES encryption keys.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] User Accounts with Unconstrained Kerberos Delegation
CustomReports.Description: Users configured with TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION flag capable of harvesting TGTs.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Accounts Flagged by AdminSDHolder (adminCount = 1)
CustomReports.Description: Accounts with adminCount=1 where ACL inheritance is stripped by AdminSDHolder.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Accounts with Populated sIDHistory
CustomReports.Description: Accounts containing migrated sIDHistory attributes that can grant unexpected historical access.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Sensitive Administrative Accounts Without Delegation Protection
CustomReports.Description: High-privilege accounts (adminCount=1) lacking the NOT_DELEGATED flag (0x100000).

CustomReports.Name: [Account Security] Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access Group Hygiene
CustomReports.Description: Memberships in the Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access group that may expose directory metadata to anonymous users.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Inactive Accounts (No Logon in 90+ Days)
CustomReports.Description: Accounts with no recorded logon activity within the last 90 days.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Dormant Accounts (No Logon in 180+ Days)
CustomReports.Description: Accounts dormant for over 6 months.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Accounts That Have Never Logged In
CustomReports.Description: Provisioned accounts where logon count is 0 or lastLogonTimestamp is missing.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Expired User Accounts Past Expiration Date
CustomReports.Description: Accounts whose accountExpires attribute is in the past.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Passwords Expiring Within 14 Days
CustomReports.Description: Accounts approaching password expiration cutoff.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Passwords Not Changed in Over 365 Days
CustomReports.Description: Accounts with static credentials unchanged for over a year.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Disabled Accounts Retaining Group Memberships
CustomReports.Description: Disabled accounts that still belong to security groups other than Domain Users.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Orphaned Accounts Without Assigned Manager
CustomReports.Description: Active employees with missing or unresolvable manager attribute.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Accounts Provisioned Within Last 30 Days
CustomReports.Description: Audit log of recently created accounts for onboarding verification.

CustomReports.Name: [Account Lifecycle] Active Accounts Missing Email or Department
CustomReports.Description: Active accounts lacking essential directory metadata.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Empty Security Groups (0 Members)
CustomReports.Description: Security groups containing zero members.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Circular Group Nesting Loops
CustomReports.Description: Groups nested in an infinite loop that degrade token size and LSASS evaluation.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Deeply Nested Groups (> 3 Levels)
CustomReports.Description: Groups nested deeper than 3 hierarchy levels causing token bloat.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Members of Built-in High-Privilege Groups
CustomReports.Description: Accounts assigned to Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, or Schema Admins.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Excessively Large Groups (> 5,000 Members)
CustomReports.Description: Large groups that generate extensive replication traffic and slow Kerberos ticket issuance.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Security Groups Without Owner (managedBy is null)
CustomReports.Description: Unowned groups lacking a designated business custodian.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Accounts with Non-Default PrimaryGroupID
CustomReports.Description: Accounts whose primaryGroupID is not 513 (Domain Users), often used for privilege concealment.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Distribution Groups Allowing Unauthenticated External Senders
CustomReports.Description: Distribution lists vulnerable to external email spoofing.

CustomReports.Name: [Group Hygiene] Groups Containing Foreign Security Principals (Cross-Forest SIDs)
CustomReports.Description: Groups with members from external domains or trusts.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Inactive Computer Accounts (No Activity in 90+ Days)
CustomReports.Description: Workstation and server accounts inactive for over 90 days.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers Running Obsolete / Unsupported Operating Systems
CustomReports.Description: Systems running Windows XP, 7, 2003, 2008, or 2012 past end of life.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers with Unconstrained Kerberos Delegation
CustomReports.Description: Non-domain controller computer accounts configured with unconstrained delegation.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers Missing LAPS Password (ms-Mcs-AdmPwd is null)
CustomReports.Description: Endpoints without Windows Local Administrator Password Solution configured.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers Missing BitLocker Recovery Keys in AD
CustomReports.Description: Client computers without BitLocker TPM recovery secrets backed up in the directory.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Stale or Unreachable Domain Controllers
CustomReports.Description: Domain controllers failing replication or showing stale logon heartbeats.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Disabled Computer Accounts Awaiting Cleanup
CustomReports.Description: Deprovisioned computers retained in active containers.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers Missing Default HOST Service Principal Names
CustomReports.Description: Computers lacking default HOST/hostname SPNs breaking Kerberos authentication.

CustomReports.Name: [Computer Health] Computers with Non-Standard Pre-Windows 2000 Names
CustomReports.Description: Computer accounts missing trailing $ in sAMAccountName.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] User Accounts with Expired Certificates in userCertificate
CustomReports.Description: Accounts publishing expired X.509 certificates in directory attributes.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Accounts Configured with AltSecurityIdentities Mappings
CustomReports.Description: Accounts with X.509 certificate mappings in altSecurityIdentities.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] ESC1 Vulnerable Certificate Templates (Client Auth + Enrollee Supplies SAN)
CustomReports.Description: Templates permitting unprivileged enrollees to specify arbitrary SAN identities.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] ESC2 Certificate Templates (Any Purpose EKU or Missing EKU)
CustomReports.Description: Templates with Any Purpose EKU or zero EKUs allowing subordinate CA impersonation.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Certificates with Weak Keys (< 2048-bit RSA)
CustomReports.Description: Certificates signed with RSA 1024-bit or weaker keys.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Missing or Incomplete NTAuthStore Enterprise CA Certificates
CustomReports.Description: Missing CA certificates in the NTAuthCertificates container causing smart card logon failures.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Restricted Enrollment Agent Templates with Broad Permissions
CustomReports.Description: Enrollment agent certificates allowed without restrictive enrollment agent constraints.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Certificate Autoenrollment Active for Inactive Accounts
CustomReports.Description: Inactive accounts continuing to automatically renew certificates.

CustomReports.Name: [PKI/Certificates] Smart Card Required Accounts with Passwords Set to Never Expire
CustomReports.Description: SMARTCARD_REQUIRED accounts where DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD flag was also set, leaving long-lived static NTLM hashes.
